text:
Sam: quick heads-up — ran a canary profile against rw-7b with long seqs and batch growth. seeing spikes that look like padding+KV cache interacting to blow up workspace usage and trigger OOMs.

Rina: can you paste the exact repro and profiler snippet? want to triage ASAP.

Sam: repro command below. this is with the kernel-switch landed last week.
```
./profiler --model rw-7b-q --batch 48 --seq 1024 --kv-enabled --runs 300
--config allocator.slab_mb=2048 --config workspace.reserve_mb=384
```
Profiler excerpt:
```
[alloc] slab=2048MB workspace_reserved=384MB
[pad] pad_ratio=0.32 tokens_wasted=230420 (23%)
[per_seq] overhead=14KB/seq
[kv] active=1.12GB evicted=320MB
[peak] peak_gpu_mem=12.10GB step=216
[oom] oom_at_step=217 allocated=12.8GB limit=12.5GB
```
Sam: note: when batch grows from 32->48 padded tokens jump non-linearly because a small number of long sequences push the padded length up, and unfused attention kernel we now select allocates a lot of temporaries per seq.

Lex: fyi the kernel selector picks `attn_unfused` for seq>=512 under current heuristic. `attn_unfused` uses extra temporaries ~600KB/seq in our CUDA kernels (temporary softmax buffers + tiled accumulators). at batch 48 that is ~28MB extra temp per step but multiplied across workspace allocation patterns it fragments into ~700MB observed.

Kai: couple of quick mitigation ideas: cap effective pad per-sample (e.g. clamp to 512) so tail sequences don't blow up batch pad; make KV eviction more aggressive for canary runs (evict LRU segments earlier); and set workspace reserve to 1.5x median instead of 2x peak to reduce precommit.

Noah: this smells like the regression we saw after kernel-switch PR (commit 8d9f2c). can we try a rollback-only canary? throughput/backpressure tradeoff is expected but we need stability.

Sam: I tried local rollback of 8d9f2c -> peak dropped ~900MB and no OOM in 300 runs, but end-to-end throughput dropped ~8% for this seq distribution.

Rina: allocator knobs we can try quickly: reduce slab chunk from 2MB->1MB, enable `buffer_reuse=true`, and disable `workspace_prefetch`. quick test on dev node saved ~300MB peak in my run. can everyone test with same profiler command?

Sam: test config I used: `allocator.slab_chunk_kb=1024, allocator.buffer_reuse=true, workspace.prefetch=false`

Lex: longer-term suggestion: kernel selector should consider seq distribution skew (p95/p99) not just avg. prefer fused kernels if skewed tail exists even when they appear slightly higher single-req latency — memory blowups are worse. also add per-kernel workspace estimator so selector can predict temp buffer cost: `est_tmp_mb = base + seq * tmp_per_token`.

Kai: also think about dynamic batching guardrails: when batch pad would increase >threshold, limit dynamic batch expansion or split into two smaller batches to reduce padding waste. small policy change but big mem win.

Noah: I opened PR to add a rollback flag and a canary pipeline: https://git.company/redwood/infra/pulls/4521 — infra will run canary-8732.

InfraBot: deploy/canary started by @Noah — cluster=canary-cluster job=canary-8732 status=running

Sam: I'll run profiler against canary once infra reports green. attaching a small flame/alloc profile next in thread.

Lex: agreed on plan: (1) run rollback canary, (2) try allocator tweaks on a parallel canary, (3) evaluate kernel-selector change for seq-skew. thanks — this explains the mysterious per-seq memory scaling we've been seeing. :thumbsup:

Sam: noted. filing an issue with logs and three experiments: rollback, allocator-tune, dynamic-batch-guard. PRs incoming.

Rina: thanks — if canary shows improvement we can schedule a controlled rollout.
